content.text:
The hypothesis is a spread of two history-standardized growth rates: pay growth minus hours growth, with a positive predicted sign. That matches claim 5, which describes a spread between two flow rates, each standardized against its own history. Claim 5 gave a positive IC with a t-stat of about 1.9, so this hypothesis appears to test or build on it.

Claim 3 concerns a cross-sectional rank product of pay growth and hours change, which is a different construction (a product, not a spread), though it uses similar variables. The hypothesis is not a product, so claim 3 is not clearly used. Claim 2 covers a product of standardized measures, so it does not match either. Claims 6 and 7 are caveats attached to the claim 5 finding (stronger in high-T periods, coverage around 54%). The hypothesis does not test them.
